title: Golden Age Gold
intro: [excited] Dust off your VHS clamshells, friends, because tonight we are traveling back to the golden age of Disney, 1937 to 1970! Snow White, Sleeping Beauty, Mary Poppins, the classics. If you were born after the year 2000, don't worry, I'll go easy on you... [mischievously] probably.

categories.title: Once Upon a Dream
categories.intro: We open with Sleeping Beauty, the 1959 masterpiece. Grab your pillow, but please... [whispers] do NOT fall asleep on me.

clues.clue: In Sleeping Beauty, Maleficent's curse says Princess Aurora will prick her finger on the spindle of one of these.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is a spinning wheel! Which is why King Stefan had every single one in the kingdom burned. [chuckles] Honestly, a BIT of an overreaction, but it is a fairy tale.

clues.clue: Flora loves pink and Fauna loves green, but this third good fairy insists that Aurora's gown should be blue.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Merryweather! The pink versus blue dress battle is still going on at the end of the movie. [laughs] I am TEAM BLUE, sorry Flora.

clues.clue: While she is hidden away in the forest cottage, Aurora goes by this flowery name.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Briar Rose! It is a nod to the Brothers Grimm version of the story, which is actually titled Little Briar Rose.

clues.clue: Much of the music in Sleeping Beauty, including Once Upon a Dream, is adapted from a ballet by this Russian composer.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Tchaikovsky! Once Upon a Dream is built on the Garland Waltz from his 1890 ballet. [chuckles] Not bad for a guy who never got a Disney paycheck.

clues.clue: Sleeping Beauty was the first animated feature shot in this super-wide 70 millimeter format.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Super Technirama 70! That giant canvas is why every background looks like a medieval tapestry. It also made the film wildly expensive. [sighs] Worth it.

categories.title: Firsts and Forevers
categories.intro: The golden age was full of firsts. Name the movie or the character that made Disney history.

clues.clue: Released in 1937, this was Walt Disney's very first full-length animated feature film.
clues.answer: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
accept: snow white and the seven dwarfs
choices: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs! Hollywood called it Disney's Folly before it came out. Then it became the highest grossing film of its time. [laughs] Who's laughing NOW?

clues.clue: The Blue Fairy appoints this character to be Pinocchio's official conscience.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Jiminy Cricket! He even got a fancy gold badge for the job. Lord High Keeper of the Knowledge of Right and Wrong. [chuckles] Put THAT on a resume.

clues.clue: This 1950 adventure about young Jim Hawkins and Long John Silver was Disney's first completely live-action feature.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Treasure Island! It was filmed in England, partly because Disney had money stuck there after the war. [mischievously] Pirates, but make it a tax strategy.

clues.clue: Released in 1955, this romance was Disney's first animated feature filmed in widescreen CinemaScope.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Lady and the Tramp! Bella Notte, a plate of spaghetti, one meatball. [sighs] The most romantic noodle in film history.

clues.clue: This 1961 film was the first Disney animated feature to use xerography throughout, copying the animators' drawings straight onto cels.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is One Hundred and One Dalmatians! [gasps] Imagine hand-inking all those spots! Xerography saved the ink department.

categories.title: Classic Couture
categories.intro: [excited] It's color palettes! I'll show you the colors of a classic character's outfit, and you tell me who is wearing them.

clues.clue: Royal blue, sunny yellow, a splash of red, and a crisp white collar. Who wears it?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Snow White! Blue bodice, yellow skirt, red bow. That outfit has not gone out of style since 1937. [chuckles] Iconic.

clues.clue: Powder blue, a white pinafore, a black hair bow, and golden hair. Who wears it?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Alice! She wore that dress through the entire trip down the rabbit hole. Not a single wardrobe change... [laughs] very low maintenance.

clues.clue: Forest green, a darker green cap, a bright red feather, and brown shoes. Who wears it?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Peter Pan! That red feather in his cap is the boy who never grows up's only accessory. [mischievously] Robin Hood fans, I see you squinting.

clues.clue: Snowy white fur, a black dress, long red gloves, and hair split right down the middle. Who wears it?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Cruella De Vil! [dramatic pause] If she doesn't scare you, no evil thing will. Fun fact, she was supposedly drawn partly from actress Tallulah Bankhead.

clues.clue: Deep purple, a black cape with a blood red lining, a tall white collar, and a gold crown. Who wears it?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Evil Queen from Snow White! [sighs] Maleficent fans, I know, I KNOW. But the high white collar and the red lining are pure Queen.

categories.title: Ride the Classics
categories.intro: To the parks! These attractions are all based on golden age films. [excited] Many of them have been delighting guests since opening day.

clues.clue: At Disneyland and Magic Kingdom, you fly over London aboard a pirate galleon on this Fantasyland dark ride.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Peter Pan's Flight! It opened with Disneyland in 1955 and still has one of the longest lines in the park. [laughs] Faith, trust, and a Lightning Lane.

media.prompt: A small wooden pirate galleon ride vehicle with billowing sails flying through a starry night sky above a miniature glowing London with a clock tower and a winding river. Original painterly storybook illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich color, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: Guests spin themselves silly in giant teacups on this Fantasyland ride, inspired by a 1951 unbirthday party.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Mad Tea Party! [mischievously] Pro tip, if you spin the wheel in the middle hard enough, your lunch will also experience an unbirthday.

clues.clue: This opening day Disneyland dark ride, based on a 1949 film, sends you on a reckless motorcar trip that ends in a very hot place.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Mr. Toad's Wild Ride! Yes, the ride literally sends you to the underworld. [chuckles] Disney in the 1950s was a LOT more metal than people remember.

clues.clue: At Disneyland, these little boats sail past miniature fairy tale villages after floating right through the mouth of Monstro the whale.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Storybook Land Canal Boats! Walt reportedly picked many of the miniatures himself. [whispers] Tiny buildings... enormous charm.

clues.clue: In 2021, Disneyland's Snow White's Scary Adventures reopened with a softer story and this new name.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Snow White's Enchanted Wish! A little less scary, a lot more sparkle. The Queen still shows up though. [laughs] She never misses a cameo.

categories.title: Golden Oldies
categories.intro: You voted for music, so here are golden age songs. Name the movie or the song. [chuckles] Singing along is encouraged, but NOT graded.

clues.clue: The Fairy Godmother sings Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Boo as she whips up a pumpkin coach in this 1950 film.
choices: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Cinderella! Put 'em together and what have you got? [excited] Two hundred easy points, that's what!

clues.clue: Baloo the bear teaches Mowgli to forget about his worries and his strife in The Bare Necessities, from this 1967 film.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is The Jungle Book! [sighs] It was the last animated feature Walt personally worked on before he passed away in 1966.

clues.clue: When You Wish Upon a Star won the Academy Award for Best Original Song for this 1940 film.
choices: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Pinocchio! Jiminy Cricket sings it, and decades later it became the Disney anthem you hear before nearly every movie.

clues.clue: Sung by Bert the chimney sweep, this Sherman Brothers song from Mary Poppins won the Oscar for Best Original Song.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Chim Chim Cher-ee! Feed the Birds was Walt's personal favorite, though. [whispers] He'd ask Richard Sherman to play it for him in his office.

clues.clue: In Dumbo, Mrs. Jumbo cradles her son through the bars of her circus wagon while this Oscar-nominated lullaby plays.
choices: When I See an Elephant Fly
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Baby Mine! [sighs] And if you didn't cry during that scene, please check your pulse. Mine is still recovering.
